sentences.text: Misc. Criminal Case No. 49797 of 2024

Mayank Singh Rajput
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Datt - Senior Advocate with Shri Hitesh Mishra
 applicant.

Shri Pramod Choubey - Govt. Advocate for respondent-State.
 Order

This is third application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.416/2023 registered at Police Station-Gadarwara, District- Narsinghpur (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC & Section 66 (c) of Information Technology Act, 2000.

2. Learned senior counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant was issued a sim card and he received a message on his mobile phone that his phone number is attached to the bank account.
Using said information, applicant has withdrawn an amount of Rs.25 Lacs from account of one Purushottam.
Learned senior counsel appearing for applicant submitted that an amount of Rs.8 Lacs has already bene seized from him and applicant is ready to deposit a further sum of Rs.8 Lacs under protest.
It is submitted that he is in jail for more than one year.
In these circumstances, he NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5930 2 MCRC-49797-2024 prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
3. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the application for grant of bail.
It is submitted that applicant has committed forgery and also cheating.
Offence is serious in nature.
In these circumstances, application for grant of bail deserves to be dismissed.

sentences.text: 4. Heard the counsel for the parties.
5. Applicant is first offender with no criminal records.
An amount of Rs.8 Lacs has already been seized from the applicant and he is ready to deposit further sum of Rs.8 Lacs under protest before the trial Court.
Investigation is complete.
Charge-sheet has been filed.
Applicant is in jail for more than one year.

6. Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, bail application stands allowed on following conditions :-
1. Applicant will furnish an FDR for sum of Rs.8,00,000/- (Rupees Eight Lacs Only)
under protest before trial Court/CJM with instruction to the Bank for renewal of FDR periodically till trial is completed.
Order shall be passed for disposal of FDR at the time of passing of final judgment by the trial Court.

7. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on aforesaid conditions on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his regular appearance before Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of trial.
as per rules.
